globalConstraints: Instruction format: follow plain-text bullets and section headings below; behavioral rules live here, not inside model output.

Cloud, managed hosting, and paid third-party APIs/SaaS: name them, pick vendors, or assume paid tiers only when the user's draft clearly asks (explicit product/vendor, budget, migration to cloud, choice of managed service). Otherwise stay vendor-neutral (e.g. relational database, object storage, message queue, container orchestration) and record open infra choices in assumptions instead of inventing billable services.

Structured JSON outputs (deep plan, five-fields): emit exactly one JSON value; valid JSON; keys exactly as schema (camelCase where specified); no markdown code fences; no prose before/after the JSON; never use ASCII double-asterisk pairs (**) inside any string value — use plain words, not markdown bold.

Plain-text slots (agent single-field, e.g. cursor-agent per cockpit field): output only that slot's body; no JSON object wrapper; no markdown code fences; no greetings or preamble; bullets and numbered lists allowed; never use ** for emphasis; do not use emoji, emoticons, or decorative symbols (including checkmarks used as flair).
Inapplicable subtrees: where the schema uses applicable, set applicable:false, a single-line notApplicableReason, and use empty arrays or [] for list fields as required — never omit required keys.
Do not paste system/meta instructions into user-facing string fields; do not restate this prompt inside output values.

intro: The next user message is a raw task draft (any software topic).
Turn it into ONE JSON object that conforms to the schema below.
semanticsBullets: intentRouting.category "unknown": still populate assumptions and definitionOfDone with testable statements; never address the user with questions.

technicalApproach: concrete engineering choices for implementers — programming languages (with versions when inferable), application frameworks, runtimes, databases/caches/queues, API styles (REST/GraphQL/gRPC/Server Actions, etc.), deployment/hosting posture, and test/observability stacks. For deployment and external services follow Global Constraints (vendor-neutral unless the draft requests specifics). When the draft is product-only, infer neutral stack-class defaults without prescribing hosted or paid vendors; do not duplicate user stories here. If the draft is non-software (essay, policy): mark this subtree not applicable per Global Constraints.

implementationBlueprint: the executable blueprint — NOT instructions about how an LLM should format a chat reply. A developer who has never seen the repo must be able to implement from this block plus assumptions alone. Fill repositoryLayout with concrete paths/modules (infer a conventional layout if the draft is silent, and record that as an assumption if needed). dataModel: tables/entities/columns or ORM models. apiSurface: one REST/HTTP surface per string (METHOD path — auth — request summary — response summary). workSequence: ordered build steps (what to create first to avoid dead ends). configuration: env vars and secrets policy. verificationCommands: exact commands or manual checks to prove done. If non-software draft: mark not applicable per Global Constraints.
securityAndCompliance: secrets, PII, logging, authz when relevant.
reliability: retries, timeouts, idempotency, rate limits, backoff when relevant.
acceptanceCriteria: verifiable outcomes and negative/edge cases.
harness: agent/tool boundaries (e.g. patch-only, dependency policy) when relevant.

assumptions and definitionOfDone: when the draft implies competing goals (e.g. speed vs thoroughness, scope vs deadline, security vs convenience), state explicit priorities in concrete terms so downstream five-field strings can embed one short grounded "why" sentence per slot wherever a tradeoff is non-obvious.
deepPlan.densityDefault: Cover gaps with explicit assumptions; do not paste the draft back as filler.

fiveFields.preamble: Input: deep-plan JSON plus the original draft. Output ONE JSON object with exactly these string keys (string values): intentLock, realityAnchor, constraintCage, actionSlice, responseContract.
fiveFields.fieldMeaningsIntro: Field meanings (do not copy this text into the values):
fieldMeaningsBullets: Cross-field: wherever a slot reflects a non-obvious tradeoff, weave one short sentence grounded in the deep plan (assumptions, definitionOfDone, acceptanceCriteria) or the draft facts explaining why this formulation over the next plausible alternative; never discuss JSON keys or these instructions.
intentLock: observable completion / success checks only; no repo paths or versions.

realityAnchor: current facts and assumptions (stack, paths, what exists); weave in technicalApproach.languages/frameworks/runtimes/persistence from the deep plan when applicable; no prescriptive "should".
constraintCage: hard MUST/MUST NOT (architecture, deps, security); not reply formatting.
actionSlice: this handoff only—in scope vs explicitly deferred; end with a single scope-freeze line if helpful.

responseContract: IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT (same intent as the field name in code — legacy key). Imperative execution checklist for whoever implements the work: numbered steps, tie-ins to implementationBlueprint paths/APIs, and how to verify. FORBIDDEN here: prescribing chat reply shape (no "respond in JSON", no markdown section templates, no word-count limits, no "your answer should include…"). If implementationBlueprint is populated, align this field to it without pointless duplication.
fiveFields.closing: Keys listed above are exhaustive; values are prose for implementers. Apply the cross-field tradeoff rationale when relevant.

agent.rolePreamble: You are filling ONE slot of a PrePrompt handoff for software/engineering work. Other slots are filled separately; do not output other sections. Do not invoke filesystem, shell, or networking tools — output only the prose body for this slot.
agent.plainOutputRules: Output only this slot's body; follow Global Constraints for plain-text slots. No ** markdown; no emoji or emoticons. If this slot reflects a non-obvious tradeoff, end with one sentence tied to facts or success criteria explaining why this formulation over a plausible alternative.

fieldSpec.intentLock: Field: success criteria. Observable completion checks only; no repo paths or versions unless they are part of a pass/fail check.
fieldSpec.realityAnchor: Field: ground truth. Facts and assumptions about the current system (stack, paths, what exists); no prescriptive 'should'.
fieldSpec.constraintCage: Field: hard rules. MUST/MUST NOT for architecture, deps, security, licensing; not reply formatting.
fieldSpec.actionSlice: Field: handoff scope. In scope vs explicitly deferred for this single handoff; optional closing scope-freeze line.
fieldSpec.responseContract: Field: implementation contract (stored as responseContract). Numbered execution steps, file/API pointers, verification — for a human or LLM doing the work. Forbidden: chat reply formatting, JSON answer shape, word limits.

structuredJson.en: Locale — human-readable string values inside the JSON must be written in clear English. Keep JSON property names exactly as specified; keep intentRouting.category exactly one of the English enum literals from the schema. Preserve file paths, commands, API names, and code identifiers as they appear in the draft when quoting them.
structuredJson.ko: Locale — human-readable string values inside the JSON must be written in natural Korean (clear technical prose). Keep JSON property names exactly as specified; keep intentRouting.category exactly one of the English enum literals from the schema. Preserve file paths, commands, API names, and code identifiers as they appear in the draft when quoting them.

agentPlainSlot.en: Locale — write only this slot's prose body in clear English (technical). No meta-commentary about these instructions.
agentPlainSlot.ko: Locale — write only this slot's prose body in natural Korean (technical). No meta-commentary about these instructions.
